newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - U.S. Santa Claus rally boosts Euro-bourses.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - U.S. Santa Claus rally boosts Euro-bourses.

text.p: European stock markets pushed strongly higher on Friday after a "Santa Claus rally" in the United States sent Wall Street surging two percent.
London's FTSE 100 index opened at a record high and Europe's other two major bourses -- Frankfurt and Paris -- joined the party, too.
"The Dow's jump overnight was unbelievable. It certainly has given the market a boost in confidence," one senior dealer in London said.

A powerful bond rally in the United States spilled over into Europe, with both British and German government bonds making a strong start. In contrast the dollar was little changed as traders headed off for their Christmas break.
The U.S. bond rally helped the Dow Jones industrial average to soar 126.87 points to 6,473.64 overnight in its second biggest point gain ever.
"This may be the start of the Santa Claus rally," said Richard Cripps, chief market strategist at Legg Mason Wood Walker.
After recent vulnerability of stock markets to big falls, Wall Street's surge came as a tonic to European bourses.
Britain's FTSE 100 index of leading shares opened 45.1 points higher at 4,096.4. Prices later slipped back on mild profit-taking, although the FTSE was still up 22 points at 4,073.4 by 1015 GMT.
"The air becomes a bit rarefied above 4,100," one market analyst said.
When the FTSE's previous intraday trading high of 4,094.4, was reached on November 26, shares quickly retreated, ending the day at 4,068.4.
But another strong showing on Wall Street may be enough to keep the FTSE above its previous closing record of 4,073.1, dealers said.

"A new closing high is definitely within sight after the Dow rally," the head of sales and trading at a large brokerage said. "An assault on the 4,100 level is also possible today but we may fall a bit short."

Car-components company GKN failed to join the pre-Christmas rally, however, falling 25.5 pence at 984 following Thursday's U.S. court ruling which may cost the company 331 million pounds ($553 million).
German shares opened floor trading strongly higher, boosted like bourses elsewhere by the Wall Street rally but also helped by a strong government bond market.
"The firm dollar, Wall Street and Bunds are all responsible for taking us into the heavens," said one dealer.
The car sector, including BMW AG, Volkswagen and Daimler-Benz, led the rally, which saw the 30-share DAX index zoom 1.7 percent to 2,855.
In Paris, shares added one percent to the CAC index in opening trades, building on Wall Street's overnight run.
Anglo-French Channel Tunnel operator Eurotunnel weakened 1.43 percent to 6.90 francs, following Thursday's small fire on a platform at the Folkestone terminal, which was quickly put out.
On foreign exchange markets, the dollar was slightly softer against the mark and slightly firmer against the yen as traders wound down ahead of the holiday.

"The dollar is ending the year on a pretty high note and the market perception at least is that fundamentals are falling into place in the short term and the U.S. economy is leading the way," said Paul Meggyesi, senior currency economist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
CURRENCIES AT 1015 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 1.5546 marks and 114.26 yen, compared with 1.5597 marks and 114.07 yen in late European business on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1015 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares wqas up 22.1 pointss, or 0.55 percent, at 4,073.4.
PARIS - The CAC-40 share index was up 27.08, or 1.2 percnet, at 2,275.78.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 47.84 points, or 1.7 percent, at 2,855.74.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold started firmer, close to the top of a $368-$370 range before meeting light selling. Silver was a cent firmer with gold at $4.88.
